column3: The Hebrew says he gives a sign or wonder, rather than proclaims one.
The Hebrew joins the sign and wonder with “and”.
The Hebrew repeats “the LORD your God” as the one they are to love.
The Hebrew retains the image of a house of slaves.
The Hebrew specifies your brother as your mother’s son and describes the friend as like your own soul.
The Hebrew describes the extent from one end of the earth to the other, rather than presenting the two ends as alternatives.
The Hebrew explicitly makes your eye the subject of showing pity.
The hand of all the people is singular in the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately says to stone him with stones and that he shall die.
The Hebrew calls the men “sons of worthlessness”.
The Hebrew explicitly says “behold” and describes the deed as established.
The Hebrew retains the mouth-of-the-sword image twice and includes everything in the city, not only people and livestock.
The Hebrew directly says the city shall not be built again.
Your hand is singular in the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says to listen to the voice of the LORD your God.
